cells.tense: The picture is already vivid for you, and you are still moving toward it.
cells.act: do the next piece at the speed you can keep for a month, not the speed you can keep for a day
cells.ask: Pick the next piece of what you are building and do it at a pace you could hold for four weeks, not one you could hold for a day. Notice what it feels like to keep moving that way.
cells.core:
You can see the whole thing already. Where most people need proof before they move, you move because you can picture it, and when the picture is vivid the momentum is easy. That is the good version: you know what you are aiming at and you enjoy the going. What bends it is the calendar. When the picture is clear you want it finished at the speed of the picture, and the doing outruns your own hunger for the result.
The slower pace holds longer here. Take the next piece and work at a pace you could keep for four weeks. Not the pace of a good Tuesday. Notice whether the momentum steadies when you stop outrunning your appetite for it. You will still get there. It just will not cost you the enjoyment on the way.
cells.sheetLine: You move because you can see it, and the pace is the work.
cells.verb: to keep imagining the whole thing through until it is fully felt
cells.place: in the momentum you carry toward what you have set your sights on

cells.tense: The whole thing needs to be finished already, or it starts to feel like it is slipping.
cells.ask: Choose the thing you are building that you would hate to lose, and take care of it this week the way a good gardener does — steady attention, no forcing. Notice where your grip is tighter than it needs to be.
cells.core:
You can see the finished version so clearly that any gap between it and now reads as a problem. So you push. What you are building gets tended hard, scheduled, second-guessed, moved forward before it has grown into itself. From the outside it looks like drive. From underneath it feels like the thing might get taken from you if you rest.
The other half of care is not gripping. For one week, tend what you would be sorriest to lose the way a good gardener tends a bed — water it, watch it, leave it alone between waterings. Notice where your hands are doing more than the thing needs. Care that does not exhaust is how this gets finished. Clutching is how it gets dropped.
cells.sheetLine: You push what you could tend, and the grip is what tires you.
cells.verb: to keep imagining the whole thing through until it is fully felt
cells.place: in the momentum you carry toward what you have set your sights on

cells.tense: You had the picture once, and getting back to it feels like something you already walked past.
cells.act: keep the truth a while before saying it
cells.ask: Pick something you are working toward that you have been quiet about, and hold it to yourself for a few days without explaining it to anyone. Put down what you know about it before you decide anything.
cells.core:
The aim used to be right there with you. Now the goals are being managed rather than reached for, and the vividness is somewhere back along the road. What you are carrying gets weighed but not moved, and the not-moving starts to look like not-wanting it. It is not that.
Do not push effort where the appetite has gone quiet — that just makes noise. Go sideways instead. Take something you are building and keep your own read on it for a few days without announcing it, without defending it, without deciding. What you know about it will sharpen if you stop demanding an answer. Then the picture has somewhere to come back to, and the appetite returns before the moving does.
cells.sheetLine: You know the aim, and you have stopped letting yourself hold it.
cells.verb: to keep imagining the whole thing through until it is fully felt
cells.place: in the momentum you carry toward what you have set your sights on

cells.tense: You are steering the whole thing well, and if someone asked who chose the course you would credit the wind.
cells.act: sort what matters from what does not, carefully
cells.ask: Take the list of what you are pushing toward right now and sort it once, carefully — what actually moves the thing, and what is only noise around it. Strike one piece of noise, and keep the list.
cells.core:
The steering is yours. You decide what gets dropped, what gets kept, what gets moved next, and when anyone asks it sounds like circumstances made the call. Things move because you keep moving them. You are the one choosing, and that has been filed under something else.
To take it back, narrow. Sort the list of what you are pushing toward into what actually moves it and what only surrounds it. Strike one piece of noise. That sounds small. It is the whole move, because sorting is you looking at your own hand. Do it once this week and notice how much of the momentum was already yours.
cells.sheetLine: The course is yours, filed under something else.
cells.verb: to keep imagining the whole thing through until it is fully felt
cells.place: in the momentum you carry toward what you have set your sights on

attempts.check: The record calls Fulfillment 'deep satisfaction in what was imagined,' but the person lives in the Drive seat — momentum toward goals — so any claim that the satisfaction is already here is unsupported; the reader could reasonably say the imagining is real but the contentment is not what they feel. The asks are each one small honest move of the medicine itself (alignment, stewardship, reflection, honing), so they survive being wrong about the diagnosis: doing the next piece at a keepable pace, tending without clutching, holding a truth before saying it, sorting what matters, all teach something regardless. The sentence that serves the writer is 'you are satisfied because what you imagined has been felt' — it is the record's own prose, and on glass it would both flatter and prophesy; I am rendering the imagining without the verdict on how it lands. Narrowed claims, one image at most, no motive read, no history invented.
